input.notes: No download: the corpus lives on Clipper and the harness opens it. See Dataset notes.

harness.notes: `./build/task solve <workdir> <result.bin> <seed>`. The harness opens the corpus, generates the initial weights and the batch order from the seed, allocates zeroed space for the answer, drops the corpus from the page cache, then times `hpcbench::solve`. Afterwards (untimed) it checks peak memory against the budget, checks the parameters are finite, computes the full-data reconstruction MSE in double precision, and writes that single number as the result.
harness.solution_signature: void hpcbench::solve(const Corpus& c, const Params& p, Result& out)

files.build.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# build.sh -- YOURS to edit. Flags, vectorisation, OpenMP, LTO: all fair game.
#
# It must produce ONE binary at build/task, linking the host harness with your
# solution:
#
#     harness.cpp        host-owned: main, the timing boundary, the checks
#     src/solution.cpp   yours, timed
#
# Your file must not define main(); the harness owns the process.
set -eu

CXX=${CXX:-c++}
CXXFLAGS=${CXXFLAGS:--O3 -std=c++17 -DNDEBUG -fno-math-errno}

f=src/solution.cpp
[ -f "$f" ] || { echo "build.sh: missing $f" >&2; exit 1; }
if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*(int|auto)[[:space:]]+main[[:space:]]*\(' "$f"; then
  echo "build.sh: $f defines main(); the harness owns main." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p build
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
$CXX $CXXFLAGS -march=native -fopenmp -Iinclude harness.cpp src/solution.cpp -o build/task
echo "built build/task with $CXX $CXXFLAGS -march=native -fopenmp"
